memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: After the plague the LORD said to Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron, the priest, "Take a census of the whole Israelite community by families—all those twenty years old or more who are able to serve in the army of Israel." So on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho, Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them and said, "Take a census of the men twenty years old or more, as the LORD commanded Moses." - Num 26:1-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The words "after the plague" carry great weight. Israel had just passed through the devastating judgment at Peor, where thousands died because of sin. And now, in the very next breath, God calls for a new census. Life goes on. God is not finished with His people, even after a season of failure and loss.

There is grace in this fresh count. God could have abandoned Israel after their rebellion, but instead He begins to prepare them for the future He had promised. The census was a step toward entering the land, a sign that God's purposes had not been derailed by the people's sin. His plan pressed forward.

Notice too the location: the plains of Moab, across from Jericho. They were now on the threshold of the Promised Land, so close to the fulfilment of what God had spoken decades earlier. After all the wandering, all the failures, God was bringing them to the edge of His promise.

This is how God works with His people. Failure is not the final word; His faithfulness is. In Christ, we too are given new beginnings after our falls, and God continues His good work in us even when we have stumbled (Phil 1:6). Whatever judgment or failure lies behind you, take heart: God's purposes for His people move steadily on.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe God can bring new beginnings after failure?
2. How does God's faithfulness continue even through our stumbles?
3. What fresh start might God be calling you toward today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You that failure is never the final word with You. After my stumbles, grant me fresh beginnings, and carry forward the good work You have begun in me through Christ. Amen.
